01 — HERO

"A story that began with strangers, and ends with family."

02 — Intro

We started with a dream.

Five years ago, we walked through these gates as students. Different people, different stories, different dreams. Somewhere along the way, those individual stories became one shared journey.

"And somewhere between the pressure, laughter, friendships and countless deadlines… we became graduates."
03 — The Journey

Five Years
In The Making

A journey we didn't fully understand until we looked back.
↓ Scroll to travel through the years
100 Level
2021 / 2022

The Seed

It started with unfamiliar faces, new surroundings, new routines, and the excitement of beginning something we knew would take years to complete.

We walked into the department as individuals.

We had no idea who would become our closest friends, which lecturers we would never forget, or just how much this place would eventually become part of our story.

We were simply beginning.

200 Level
2022 / 2023

The Roots

By now, the faces were no longer unfamiliar.

Names became friends. Friends became familiar faces in every lecture, every group discussion, every assignment, and every class meeting.

Somewhere along the way, we stopped feeling like a group of students who happened to share a department.

We were becoming a class.

The roots were taking hold.

300 Level
2023 / 2024

The Growth

Then the journey began to demand more from us.

The courses became heavier. The responsibilities increased. The expectations grew.

There were more assignments, more presentations, more examinations, more field experiences, and more reasons to ask:

"Who has the material?" … "Past Questions Send Abeg."

Somehow, between the pressure and the laughter, we kept moving forward.

And without realizing it, we were becoming the people we came here to become.

400 Level
2024 / 2025

The Storm

Then came the year we would all come to know as ASPP.

Jeez.

We had heard about this year before we got there. We had heard the stories, the warnings, the pressure, and the endless talk about what awaited us.

But hearing about it was one thing.
Living it was another.

ASPP tested more than our academic strength. It tested our patience, our friendships, our relationships, and sometimes even our ability to stay in the same group chat without drama. 😂

It was the year we discovered who would stand by us, who would disappear when things got difficult, and, yes, who we probably should have kept at a safe distance.

Cliques formed. Friendships changed. There were misunderstandings, quarrels, silent treatments, reconciliations, and a few stories that probably deserve their own documentary.

Some disagreements were settled.
Some weren't.

But somehow, the class kept moving.

Through the pressure, the late nights, the complaints, the laughter, the endless academic battles, and the legendary:

"Emadou again? Farm again?" 😂

We made it through.
We didn't always agree.
We didn't always understand each other.
We didn't always have it figured out.
But we kept showing up.

And somehow, through all the storms, we crossed it together.

500 Level
2026

The Harvest

And then, somehow, we arrived at the final chapter.

The finish line that once felt so far away was suddenly right in front of us.

But 500 Level came with its own kind of epic pressure — like ehn.

Research.
Data collection.
Analysis.
Project writing.
Corrections.
Defense.
Final examinations.
Clearance.

And, the animal department and soil their own ASPP never ended — there was still farming, practical work, poultry rearing, and one way or another, ASPP still finding a way to remind us that it wasn't completely finished with us. Only the World Bankers were free from the ASPP chains — Agricultural Economics and Extension. 😂

There were deadlines to meet, projects to complete, data to chase, corrections to make, and moments when we wondered how everything would somehow come together.

But it did.

One task at a time.
One deadline at a time.
One final hurdle after another.

And then, the things we had spent years talking about finally became reality.

The last examination.
The final defense.
The final clearance.
The final signature.

Done.

Five years. Five years of lectures, friendships, field experiences, assignments, examinations, laughter, pressure, mistakes, growth, and memories that will stay with us long after the classroom is behind us.

We entered this department as students wondering what the next five years would bring.

Now, we stand at the end of the journey with a story of our own.

And then came the moment we had been waiting for.

Graduation.
The harvest of five years of planting, growing, learning, and becoming.
The degree is complete.
But the journey is just beginning.
The Harvest Is Here.
Class of 2026.
2026

Five years gave us a story.

But a story is never just about the years.

It's about the people who lived them.

08 — The Appreciation

We Did Not Walk
This Road Alone.

This one isn't about us. It's about everyone who carried us here.

🔒

Locked

This chapter opens on 29 September 2026 — the same day everything else does. Some things are worth waiting for.

Sec
To Our Lecturers

To the lecturers who taught us, challenged us, corrected us, encouraged us, and sometimes tested the very limits of our patience — thank you.

For every lecture, every practical, every field trip, every assignment, every correction, every question, and every lesson that went beyond the classroom, we are grateful.

You gave us more than course content. You gave us knowledge, discipline, perspective, and experiences that will remain with us long after the final examination.

↓
To Our Supervisors

To our supervisors and everyone who guided us through our research and final year projects — thank you for the patience, corrections, questions, recommendations, and countless revisions.

From the first idea to data collection, analysis, writing, corrections, and defense, you helped turn uncertainty into something we could finally call our own.

↓
To Our Families

To our families — our parents, siblings, relatives, and everyone who stood behind us — this achievement belongs to you too.

Thank you for the sacrifices we saw and the ones we may never fully know about.

Thank you for the calls, the encouragement, the financial support, the prayers, the food, the patience, and the countless ways you made it possible for us to keep going.

There were days when school demanded more from us than we thought we had to give. And somehow, there was always someone reminding us to keep going.

↓
To Our Friends

Thank you for making the journey lighter. For the laughter between lectures. The random conversations. The last-minute discussions. The shared materials.

The complaints about assignments. The panic before examinations. The jokes that somehow survived even the most stressful semesters. And for simply being there.

↓
To Our Class

Thank you for five years of memories. We were not always the same. We did not always agree. We had different personalities, different ambitions, different friendships, different struggles, and different ways of navigating university life.

But we shared the same classrooms. The same deadlines. The same examinations. The same field experiences. The same ASPP. The same final-year pressure. And eventually, the same finish line.

There were moments when five years felt endless. Now, somehow, we are looking back at them. And perhaps that is the strangest part of all.

The lectures are becoming memories. The assignments are becoming stories. The examinations are becoming something we survived. The projects are becoming something we can finally put behind our names.

And the people we met along the way are becoming part of a chapter we will carry with us wherever we go.

↓

So, to everyone who played a part in this journey — whether your contribution was large or small, whether you knew it at the time or not — thank you.

We may be the ones receiving the degrees. But we did not get here alone.

The Harvest Is Here.

We made it.
